I farm 10.1 mu with only two people in the household, and some labor is tied up off-farm, so I will keep the plan simple, familiar, and not too labor-heavy. Since I have 40 years of experience and well irrigation, I will stay with the wheat-maize system on most of the land because it is the steadiest way for me to secure grain output and spread risk across the year. I will put 8.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 8.0 mu, and I will keep 2.1 mu in cotton for cash income. I do not want to gamble on low-input traditional seed, so I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize and cotton seed. I will fertilize wheat more heavily because it responds well on my irrigated land and sets up the rotation well; maize will get strong nitrogen too but a bit less phosphorus than wheat; cotton will get balanced fertilizer but not as much water as the grain crops. Because I have well irrigation, I will plan around a few timely irrigations instead of many, since water and labor both cost money. I will use rotary tillage because it is quicker and fits my scale better than deep ploughing, and it is easier for me to manage across all plots. I will spray only as much as needed to keep weeds, insects, and common diseases under control, aiming for stable yield rather than chasing the absolute maximum.
